events.title: Australian Market Significantly Lower
events.description: The Australian stock market is trading significantly lower on Friday, extending the slight losses in the previous session, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is falling well below the 9,100 level, with weakness in mining, financial and technology stocks partially offset by gains in energy stocks.

events.title: Taiwan Stock Market May Extend Thursday's Losses
events.description: The Taiwan stock market on Thursday halted the three-day winning streak in which it had rallied almost 3,550 points or 8.6 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just beneath the 43,100-point plateau and it's tipped to open in the red again on Friday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market May Take Further Damage On Friday
events.description: The Singapore stock market on Thursday snapped the two-day winning streak in which it had improved more than 110 points or 2.1 percent. The Straits Times Index now sits just above the 5,280-point plateau and the losses may accelerate on Friday.

events.title: Losing Streak May Continue For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, slipping more than 50 points or 3.1 percent in that span. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just above the 1,585-point plateau and it's likely to open under water again on Friday.

events.title: Japan Stock Market May See Continued Consolidation
events.description: The Japan stock market on Thursday ended the three-day winning streak in which it had jumped almost 3,800 points or 5 percent. The Nikkei 225 now sits just beneath the 60,820-point plateau and it may extend its losses on Friday.

events.title: Tech Pressure May Weigh On South Korea Shares
events.description: The South Korea stock market on Thursday snapped the two-day winning streak in which it had surged more than 350 points or 7 percent. The KOSPI now sits just above the 5,340-point plateau and it may take further damage on Friday.

events.title: Hong Kong GDP Data Due On Friday
events.description: Hong Kong will on Friday release Q3 figures for gross domestic product, highlighting a light day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Advances As Hopes Of U.S.-Iran Deal Diminish After Trump's Message
events.description: The U.S. Dollar value edged higher on Thursday as oil supply disruption concerns returned to markets after U.S. President Donald Trump stated that the U.S. is no longer interested in a deal with Iran. With worries of inflation and global rate hikes returning, expectations among investors about an early reopening of the Strait of Hormuz vanished.

events.title: New Zealand Manufacturing PMI Fades To 54.9 In October - BusinessNZ
events.description: The manufacturing sector in New Zealand continued to expand in October, albeit at a slower pace, the latest survey from BusinessNZ revealed on Friday with a Performance of Manufacturing Index score of 54.9.

events.title: South Korea Export Prices Surge 36.7% On Year In October
events.description: Export prices in South Korea spiked 36.7 percent on year in October, the Bank of Korea said on Friday - slowing from 41.3 percent in September.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Moderately Higher
events.description: The Switzerland stock market closed on a firm note on Thursday after moving in a narrow range modestly above the flat line throught the session session.

events.title: Major European Markets Close Modestly Higher
events.description: European markets pared early gains and despite slipping into negative territory a little past mid afternoon, recovered to close modestly higher on Thursday thanks to some brisk buying at several counters in the final hour.

events.title: Canadian Market Remains Weak Despite Coming Off Early Lows
events.description: Despite coming off early lows, the Canadian market is down firmly in negative territory a little past noon on Thursday with stocks from materials and healthcare sectors continuing to reel under selling pressure.
